title: Strong coupling between antiferromagnetic magnons and spoof surface plasmons
authors: Yamin Sun, Ka Shen, H. Y. Yuan
abstract: Hybrid magnonic system provides a versatile platform for coherent information exchange between spin excitations and other physical degrees of freedom. While strong coupling between magnons and spoof plasmons has been observed based on ferrimagnetic spheres and localized microwave resonators, it remains unexplored whether coherent magnon-plasmon coupling can be achieved in planar magnetic structures. Here we study the hybridization of antiferromagnetic (AFM) magnons and spoof surface plasmons in a planar heterostructure consisting of an AFM thin film, a dielectric spacer, and a structured metal surface. By analytically solving the coupled Maxwell and magnetization dynamics equation, we predict strong magnon-plasmon coupling in the terahertz regime, manifested by pronounced avoided crossings in the dispersion. The coupling originates from the spatial overlap between magnonic and plasmonic modes in the dielectric spacer, and can be efficiently tuned through geometric parameters of the system. The calculated cooperativity confirms that the hybrid system can operate in the strong coupling regime, enabling coherent information transfer between magnons and plasmons. Our results establish a planar platform for plasmon-magnon hybridization, which is more amenable to on-chip manipulation and integration.
summary: This theoretical study predicts strong coherent coupling between antiferromagnetic magnons and spoof surface plasmons within a novel planar heterostructure. By solving coupled Maxwell and magnetization dynamics equations, the authors confirm the existence of hybrid modes exhibiting avoided crossings in the THz regime. This work presents a highly tunable platform for on-chip quantum information transfer between spin and electromagnetic excitations.
main_problem: The study investigates achieving strong, coherent information exchange between antiferromagnetic (AFM) magnons and spoof surface plasmons in a planar geometry.
main_result: The authors predict strong magnon-plasmon coupling in the terahertz regime for this planar heterostructure, confirming operation in the strong coupling regime via calculated cooperativity values exceeding unity.
method: The analysis involves analytically solving coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations to derive the system's dispersion relation.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a planar heterostructure comprising an AFM thin film, a dielectric spacer, and a structured metal surface supporting spoof surface plasmons (SSPs).
key_observables: Pronounced avoided crossings in the dispersion relation, coupling strength ($g$), and cooperativity parameter ($C$).
important_parameters: The system is tunable via geometric parameters such as groove width-to-period ratio ($a/p$), dielectric thickness ($h$), and groove depth ($d$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include assuming small-amplitude AFM oscillations and using an effective-medium approach for the corrugated metal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the planar structure, bare plasmon dispersions, and the resulting hybrid excitation dispersion curves showing avoided crossings.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the coupled electromagnetic and magnetization dynamics equations, deriving the determinant equation for the dispersion relation, and finally analyzing the coupling strength and cooperativity parameter to confirm strong coupling.
why_interesting: This work establishes a planar, chip-compatible platform for hybrid magnon-plasmon interactions, which is highly relevant for developing integrated quantum devices that couple spin excitations (magnons) with electromagnetic modes (plasmons).

Figure 3(d) shows the coupling strength decreases monotonically with increasing the dielectric thickness h. Since both surface plasmons and the AFM magnons are localized near the interface, their coupling is mediated by the overlap of their evanescent fields inside the di- electric spacer. Increasing the dielectric thickness re- duces this mode overlap and therefore weakens the co- herent coupling. For the AFM material studies here, the magnon-plasmon coupling strength can exceed 100 GHz by adjusting the geometric parameters, which in- dicates a substantially efficient energy exchange between the two modes.
